summary: Attached images are scaled to at most 2048 px and re-encoded (JPEG 0.85, a small PNG stays PNG, EXIF orientation applied then dropped, a GIF sent as is or refused), stepping down to 1600 px and 1280 px at 0.75 until each fits what is left of the unchanged 3 MiB message limit. Refusals name the image and the reason. One rule set in src/shared/image-resize.ts, ported to Kotlin.

storageDataMigration.reason: Only the bytes written for a new attachment change; the draft and outbox schemas, and the backend limit in validateUserMessageImages, are unchanged. Drafts and queued turns staged before the update are sent as they are.

automated: vitest: tests/unit/image-resize.test.ts (steps, PNG/JPEG choice, budget fit, GIF rule, refusal copy) and tests/unit/mobile-images.test.ts.
Android: ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest (ImageResizePlanTest, PrivateComposerAttachmentStagerTest, ComposerDraftCoordinatorTest) and lintDebug.
notExercised: Attaching a real 12 MP and a 50 MP photo, a rotated photo, a screenshot and a GIF on an iPhone and an Android phone.
expo-image-manipulator needs a new Expo binary (APK lane); the fingerprint runtimeVersion keeps the OTA away from older binaries.
Pasting or dropping a large image on the desktop; the canvas path has no unit test (vitest has no canvas).
